audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Sabbath healing, banquet humility, inviting poor/disabled, great banquet parable, cost of discipleship, tower/king images, and salt.

verses.restored: It happened when he went into the house of one of the rulers of the Pharisees on a Sabbath to eat bread, they were watching him closely.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as he went into the house of one of the chief Pharisees to eat bread on the sabbath day, that they watched him.

modern.text: One Sabbath, Jesus went to eat in the home of a leading Pharisee, and those in attendance were watching Him closely.

original.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἐλθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς οἶκόν τινος τῶν ἀρχόντων τῶν Φαρισαίων σαββάτῳ φαγεῖν ἄρτον καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦσαν παρατηρούμενοι αὐτόν.

verses.restored: Look, a certain man with swelling was before him.

familiar.text: And, behold, there was a certain man before him which had the dropsy.

modern.text: Right there before Him was a man with dropsy.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνθρωπός τις ἦν ὑδρωπικὸς ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Jesus answered the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or not?

familiar.text: And Jesus answering spake unto the lawyers and Pharisees, saying, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?

modern.text: So Jesus asked the experts in the law and the Pharisees, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath or not?”

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς τοὺς νομικοὺς καὶ Φαρισαίους λέγων· ⸀Ἔξεστιν τῷ σαββάτῳ ⸂θεραπεῦσαι ἢ οὔ⸃;

verses.restored: But they were silent. Taking hold of him, he healed him and released him.

familiar.text: And they held their peace. And he took him, and healed him, and let him go;

modern.text: But they remained silent. Then Jesus took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him on his way.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἡσύχασαν. καὶ ἐπιλαβόμενος ἰάσατο αὐτὸν καὶ ἀπέλυσεν.

verses.restored: He said to them, Which of you, having a child or ox fallen into a well, will not immediately pull it out on a Sabbath day?

familiar.text: And answered them, saying, Which of you shall have an ass or an ox fallen into a pit, and will not straightway pull him out on the sabbath day?

modern.text: And He asked them, “Which of you whose son or ox falls into a pit on the Sabbath day will not immediately pull him out?”

original.text: ⸀καὶ πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν· Τίνος ὑμῶν υἱὸς ἢ βοῦς εἰς φρέαρ ⸀πεσεῖται, καὶ οὐκ εὐθέως ἀνασπάσει αὐτὸν ⸀ἐν ἡμέρᾳ τοῦ σαββάτου;

verses.restored: They were not able to answer these things.

familiar.text: And they could not answer him again to these things.

modern.text: And they were unable to answer these questions. The Parable of the Guests

original.text: καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσαν ⸀ἀνταποκριθῆναι πρὸς ταῦτα.

verses.restored: He spoke a parable to those invited, noticing how they were choosing the first places, saying to them,

familiar.text: And he put forth a parable to those which were bidden, when he marked how they chose out the chief rooms; saying unto them,

modern.text: When Jesus noticed how the guests chose the places of honor, He told them a parable:

original.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς κεκλημένους παραβολήν, ἐπέχων πῶς τὰς πρωτοκλισίας ἐξελέγοντο, λέγων πρὸς αὐτούς·

verses.restored: When you are invited by someone to a wedding feast, do not recline in the first place, lest someone more honorable than you has been invited by him.

familiar.text: When thou art bidden of any man to a wedding, sit not down in the highest room; lest a more honourable man than thou be bidden of him;

modern.text: “When you are invited to a wedding banquet, do not sit in the place of honor, in case someone more distinguished than you has been invited.

original.text: Ὅταν κληθῇς ὑπό τινος εἰς γάμους, μὴ κατακλιθῇς εἰς τὴν πρωτοκλισίαν, μήποτε ἐντιμότερός σου ᾖ κεκλημένος ὑπʼ αὐτοῦ

verses.restored: The one who invited you both will come and say to you, Give this one place; then with shame you will begin to take the last place.

familiar.text: And he that bade thee and him come and say to thee, Give this man place; and thou begin with shame to take the lowest room.

modern.text: Then the host who invited both of you will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your seat.’ And in humiliation, you will have to take the last place.

original.text: καὶ ἐλθὼν ὁ σὲ καὶ αὐτὸν καλέσας ἐρεῖ σοι· Δὸς τούτῳ τόπον, καὶ τότε ἄρξῃ μετὰ αἰσχύνης τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον κατέχειν.

verses.restored: But when you are invited, go recline in the last place, so that when the one who invited you comes, he may say, Friend, move up higher; then there will be glory for you before all reclining with you.

familiar.text: But when thou art bidden, go and sit down in the lowest room; that when he that bade thee cometh, he may say unto thee, Friend, go up higher: then shalt thou have worship in the presence of them that sit at meat with thee.

modern.text: But when you are invited, go and sit in the last place, so that your host will come and tell you, ‘Friend, move up to a better place.’ Then you will be honored in front of everyone at the table with you.

original.text: ἀλλʼ ὅταν κληθῇς πορευθεὶς ἀνάπεσε εἰς τὸν ἔσχατον τόπον, ἵνα ὅταν ἔλθῃ ὁ κεκληκώς σε ⸀ἐρεῖ σοι· Φίλε, προσανάβηθι ἀνώτερον· τότε ἔσται σοι δόξα ἐνώπιον ⸀πάντων τῶν συνανακειμένων σοι.

verses.restored: For everyone exalting oneself will be humbled, and the one humbling oneself will be exalted.

familiar.text: For whosoever exalteth himself shall be abased; and he that humbleth himself shall be exalted.

modern.text: For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and the one who humbles himself will be exalted.”

original.text: ὅτι πᾶς ὁ ὑψῶν ἑαυτὸν ταπεινωθήσεται καὶ ὁ ταπεινῶν ἑαυτὸν ὑψωθήσεται.

verses.restored: He also said to the one who had invited him, When you make a lunch or dinner, do not call your friends, brothers, relatives, or rich neighbors, lest they also invite you back and repayment come to you.

familiar.text: Then said he also to him that bade him, When thou makest a dinner or a supper, call not thy friends, nor thy brethren, neither thy kinsmen, nor thy rich neighbours; lest they also bid thee again, and a recompence be made thee.

modern.text: Then Jesus said to the man who had invited Him, “When you host a dinner or a banquet, do not invite your friends or brothers or relatives or rich neighbors. Otherwise, they may invite you in return, and you will be repaid.

original.text: Ἔλεγεν δὲ καὶ τῷ κεκληκότι αὐτόν· Ὅταν ποιῇς ἄριστον ἢ δεῖπνον, μὴ φώνει τοὺς φίλους σου μηδὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς σου μηδὲ τοὺς συγγενεῖς σου μηδὲ γείτονας πλουσίους, μήποτε καὶ αὐτοὶ ⸂ἀντικαλέσωσίν σε⸃ καὶ γένηται ⸂ἀνταπόδομά σοι⸃.

verses.restored: But when you make a banquet, call poor people, disabled people, lame people, blind people.

familiar.text: But when thou makest a feast, call the poor, the maimed, the lame, the blind:

modern.text: But when you host a banquet, invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind,

original.text: ἀλλʼ ὅταν ⸂δοχὴν ποιῇς⸃, κάλει πτωχούς, ἀναπείρους, χωλούς, τυφλούς·

verses.restored: You will be blessed/flourishing, because they do not have means to repay you; for you will be repaid in the resurrection of the righteous.

familiar.text: And thou shalt be blessed; for they cannot recompense thee: for thou shalt be recompensed at the resurrection of the just.

modern.text: and you will be blessed. Since they cannot repay you, you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.” The Parable of the Banquet (Matthew 22:1–14)

original.text: καὶ μακάριος ἔσῃ, ὅτι οὐκ ἔχουσιν ἀνταποδοῦναί σοι, ἀνταποδοθήσεται γάρ σοι ἐν τῇ ἀναστάσει τῶν δικαίων.

verses.restored: One of those reclining with him heard these things and said to him, Blessed/flourishing is whoever eats bread in the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: And when one of them that sat at meat with him heard these things, he said unto him, Blessed is he that shall eat bread in the kingdom of God.

modern.text: When one of those reclining with Him heard this, he said to Jesus, “Blessed is everyone who will eat at the feast in the kingdom of God.”

original.text: Ἀκούσας δέ τις τῶν συνανακειμένων ταῦτα εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Μακάριος ⸀ὅστις φάγεται ⸀ἄρτον ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: He said to him, A certain person made a great dinner and invited many.

familiar.text: Then said he unto him, A certain man made a great supper, and bade many:

modern.text: But Jesus replied, “A certain man prepared a great banquet and invited many guests.

original.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἄνθρωπός τις ⸀ἐποίει δεῖπνον μέγα, καὶ ἐκάλεσεν πολλούς,

verses.restored: At the hour of the dinner he sent his servant to say to those invited, Come, because now it is ready.

familiar.text: And sent his servant at supper time to say to them that were bidden, Come; for all things are now ready.

modern.text: When it was time for the banquet, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, for everything is now ready.’

original.text: καὶ ἀπέστειλεν τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ τῇ ὥρᾳ τοῦ δείπνου εἰπεῖν τοῖς κεκλημένοις· Ἔρχεσθε, ὅτι ἤδη ἕτοιμά ⸀ἐστιν.

verses.restored: They all alike began to excuse themselves. The first said, I bought a field, and I have necessity to go out and see it; I ask you, have me excused.

familiar.text: And they all with one consent began to make excuse. The first said unto him, I have bought a piece of ground, and I must needs go and see it: I pray thee have me excused.

modern.text: But one after another they all began to make excuses. The first one said, ‘I have bought a field, and I need to go see it. Please excuse me.’

original.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀπὸ μιᾶς ⸂πάντες παραιτεῖσθαι⸃. ὁ πρῶτος εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀγρὸν ἠγόρασα καὶ ἔχω ἀνάγκην ⸀ἐξελθὼν ἰδεῖν αὐτόν· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

verses.restored: Another said, I bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to test them; I ask you, have me excused.

familiar.text: And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I go to prove them: I pray thee have me excused.

modern.text: Another said, ‘I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them out. Please excuse me.’

original.text: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Ζεύγη βοῶν ἠγόρασα πέντε καὶ πορεύομαι δοκιμάσαι αὐτά· ἐρωτῶ σε, ἔχε με παρῃτημένον.

verses.restored: Another said, I married a wife, and because of this I am not able to come.

familiar.text: And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot come.

modern.text: Still another said, ‘I have married a wife, so I cannot come.’

original.text: καὶ ἕτερος εἶπεν· Γυναῖκα ἔγημα καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὐ δύναμαι ἐλθεῖν.

verses.restored: The servant came and reported these things to his lord. Then the house-master, angered, said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, disabled, blind, and lame.

familiar.text: So that servant came, and shewed his lord these things. Then the master of the house being angry said to his servant, Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor, and the maimed, and the halt, and the blind.

modern.text: The servant returned and reported all this to his master. Then the owner of the house became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and alleys of the city, and bring in the poor, the crippled, the blind, and the lame.’

original.text: καὶ παραγενόμενος ὁ ⸀δοῦλος ἀπήγγειλεν τῷ κυρίῳ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα. τότε ὀργισθεὶς ὁ οἰκοδεσπότης εἶπεν τῷ δούλῳ αὐτοῦ· Ἔξελθε ταχέως εἰς τὰς πλατείας καὶ ῥύμας τῆς πόλεως, καὶ τοὺς πτωχοὺς καὶ ἀναπείρους καὶ ⸂τυφλοὺς καὶ χωλοὺς⸃ εἰσάγαγε ὧδε.

verses.restored: The servant said, Lord, what you commanded has happened, and still there is place.

familiar.text: And the servant said, Lord, it is done as thou hast commanded, and yet there is room.

modern.text: ‘Sir,’ the servant replied, ‘what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.’

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ δοῦλος· Κύριε, γέγονεν ⸀ὃ ἐπέταξας, καὶ ἔτι τόπος ἐστίν.

verses.restored: The lord said to the servant, Go out into the roads and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house may be filled.

familiar.text: And the lord said unto the servant, Go out into the highways and hedges, and compel them to come in, that my house may be filled.

modern.text: So the master told his servant, ‘Go out to the highways and hedges and compel them to come in, so that my house will be full.

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν ὁ κύριος πρὸς τὸν δοῦλον· Ἔξελθε εἰς τὰς ὁδοὺς καὶ φραγμοὺς καὶ ἀνάγκασον εἰσελθεῖν, ἵνα γεμισθῇ ⸂μου ὁ οἶκος⸃·

verses.restored: For I say to you that none of those people who were invited will taste my dinner.

familiar.text: For I say unto you, That none of those men which were bidden shall taste of my supper.

modern.text: For I tell you, not one of those men who were invited will taste my banquet.’” The Cost of Discipleship (Matthew 8:18–22; Luke 9:57–62; John 6:59–66)

original.text: λέγω γὰρ ὑμῖν ὅτι οὐδεὶς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐκείνων τῶν κεκλημένων γεύσεταί μου τοῦ ⸀δείπνου.

verses.restored: Great crowds were traveling with him, and turning, he said to them,

familiar.text: And there went great multitudes with him: and he turned, and said unto them,

modern.text: Large crowds were now traveling with Jesus, and He turned and said to them,

original.text: Συνεπορεύοντο δὲ αὐτῷ ὄχλοι πολλοί, καὶ στραφεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς·

verses.restored: If anyone comes to me and does not hate father, mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters, and even one's own life/soul, that one is not able to be my disciple.

familiar.text: If any man come to me, and hate not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brethren, and sisters, yea, and his own life also, he cannot be my disciple.

modern.text: “If anyone comes to Me and does not hate his father and mother and wife and children and brothers and sisters—yes, even his own life—he cannot be My disciple.

original.text: Εἴ τις ἔρχεται πρός με καὶ οὐ μισεῖ τὸν πατέρα ⸀ἑαυτοῦ καὶ τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὴν γυναῖκα καὶ τὰ τέκνα καὶ τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τὰς ἀδελφάς, ἔτι ⸀τε καὶ τὴν ⸂ψυχὴν ἑαυτοῦ⸃, οὐ δύναται ⸂εἶναί μου μαθητής⸃.

verses.restored: Whoever does not carry one's own cross and come after me is not able to be my disciple.

familiar.text: And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.

modern.text: And whoever does not carry his cross and follow Me cannot be My disciple.

original.text: ⸀ὅστις οὐ βαστάζει τὸν σταυρὸν ⸀ἑαυτοῦ καὶ ἔρχεται ὀπίσω μου, οὐ δύναται εἶναί μου μαθητής.

verses.restored: For which of you, wanting to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate the cost, whether one has enough for completion?

familiar.text: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?

modern.text: Which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and count the cost to see if he has the resources to complete it?

original.text: τίς γὰρ ἐξ ⸀ὑμῶν θέλων πύργον οἰκοδομῆσαι οὐχὶ πρῶτον καθίσας ψηφίζει τὴν δαπάνην, εἰ ⸀ἔχει εἰς ἀπαρτισμόν;

verses.restored: Otherwise, after laying a foundation and not being strong enough to finish, all seeing may begin to mock him,

familiar.text: Lest haply, after he hath laid the foundation, and is not able to finish it, all that behold it begin to mock him,

modern.text: Otherwise, if he lays the foundation and is unable to finish the work, everyone who sees it will ridicule him,

original.text: ἵνα μήποτε θέντος αὐτοῦ θεμέλιον καὶ μὴ ἰσχύοντος ἐκτελέσαι πάντες οἱ θεωροῦντες ἄρξωνται ⸂αὐτῷ ἐμπαίζειν⸃

verses.restored: saying, This person began to build and was not strong enough to finish.

familiar.text: Saying, This man began to build, and was not able to finish.

modern.text: saying, ‘This man could not finish what he started to build.’

original.text: λέγοντες ὅτι Οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἤρξατο οἰκοδομεῖν καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν ἐκτελέσαι.

verses.restored: Or what king, going to engage another king in battle, will not first sit down and deliberate whether he is able with ten thousand to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?

familiar.text: Or what king, going to make war against another king, sitteth not down first, and consulteth whether he be able with ten thousand to meet him that cometh against him with twenty thousand?

modern.text: Or what king on his way to war with another king will not first sit down and consider whether he can engage with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?

original.text: ἢ τίς βασιλεὺς πορευόμενος ⸂ἑτέρῳ βασιλεῖ συμβαλεῖν⸃ εἰς πόλεμον οὐχὶ καθίσας πρῶτον ⸀βουλεύσεται εἰ δυνατός ἐστιν ἐν δέκα χιλιάσιν ⸀ὑπαντῆσαι τῷ μετὰ εἴκοσι χιλιάδων ἐρχομένῳ ἐπʼ αὐτόν;

verses.restored: If not, while the other is still far away, he sends a delegation and asks the things for peace.

familiar.text: Or else, while the other is yet a great way off, he sendeth an ambassage, and desireth conditions of peace.

modern.text: And if he is unable, he will send a delegation while the other king is still far off, to ask for terms of peace.

original.text: εἰ δὲ μήγε, ἔτι ⸂αὐτοῦ πόρρω⸃ ὄντος πρεσβείαν ἀποστείλας ἐρωτᾷ ⸀τὰ πρὸς εἰρήνην.

verses.restored: So therefore, every one of you who does not renounce all one's possessions is not able to be my disciple.

familiar.text: So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.

modern.text: In the same way, any one of you who does not give up everything he has cannot be My disciple. Good Salt (Matthew 5:13–16; Mark 9:49–50)

original.text: οὕτως οὖν πᾶς ἐξ ὑμῶν ὃς οὐκ ἀποτάσσεται πᾶσιν τοῖς ἑαυτοῦ ὑπάρχουσιν οὐ δύναται ⸂εἶναί μου⸃ μαθητής.

verses.restored: Salt is beautiful/good; but if even salt becomes tasteless, with what will it be seasoned?

familiar.text: Salt is good: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be seasoned?

modern.text: Salt is good, but if the salt loses its savor, with what will it be seasoned?

original.text: Καλὸν ⸀οὖν τὸ ἅλας· ἐὰν δὲ ⸀καὶ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ, ἐν τίνι ἀρτυθήσεται;

verses.restored: It is useful neither for soil nor for manure pile; they throw it outside. Whoever has ears to hear, let that one hear.

familiar.text: It is neither fit for the land, nor yet for the dunghill; but men cast it out. He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

modern.text: It is fit neither for the soil nor for the manure pile, and it is thrown out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.”

original.text: οὔτε εἰς γῆν οὔτε εἰς κοπρίαν εὔθετόν ἐστιν· ἔξω βάλλουσιν αὐτό. ὁ ἔχων ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
